impact_scope.description: The existing getaddrinfo path changes when parallel address-family retries are terminated: a successful response now stops the other query's retries only after accumulated results contain IPv4. The new helper merely implements this internal decision.

evidence: In S0, host_callback already processed the parallel lookup responses and could call terminate_retries after a successful parse.
H0 exercises DNS record parsing/writing and ares_set_servers_csv, but never invokes the existing ares_getaddrinfo_int/getaddrinfo lifecycle needed to reach this retry decision.
In S1, the identical getaddrinfo lifecycle reaches the modified condition in host_callback; ai_has_ipv4 is an internal helper and requires no direct harness call.
H0 remains unable to exercise this path because it still does not initiate getaddrinfo requests or drive their asynchronous response and retry lifecycle.

new_harness_obligation.description: The commit changes an internal retry predicate on an existing callable path. Exercising it still requires the same getaddrinfo entry and asynchronous response ordering already required in S0; no new entry point, caller-supplied value or buffer, configuration, or call-order control is introduced.
evidence: ares_getaddrinfo_int has the same declaration in S0 and S1.
host_callback receives no new caller-controlled argument, and ai_has_ipv4 derives its result automatically from the existing accumulated addrinfo nodes.

reason: The same omitted getaddrinfo lifecycle has an exposure gap on both sides. The new IPv4-dependent retry decision is internal behavior reached through that unchanged lifecycle, so it does not create or aggravate a caller-visible harness obligation.
